result:
All six deliverables are done. Everything below was run in the foreground to completion.

## D1 — trigger and version

**`git` 2.55.0.** git sets `Content-Encoding: gzip` when the request body is **larger than 1,024 bytes**. 1,024 → plain, 1,025 → gzip. Bracketed to the byte on both protocols by padding `GIT_USER_AGENT`, which git copies verbatim into the `agent=` pkt-line inside the body — one character in, one body byte out. That's the re-derivation recipe.

- Not dependent on `protocol.version`: same 1,024/1,025 boundary on v0 and v2.
- Not dependent on `http.postBuffer`: 500 MB changes nothing. Below the body size git switches to the large-request path (4-byte probe + chunked, **uncompressed**), so gzip and that path are mutually exclusive. On v2, `http.postBuffer` under 65516 makes git 2.55 abort with `BUG: remote-curl.c:1533`.
- Repro at `b53e06f`: 200-ref clone, v0 body 5,142 gzip → 400, v2 body 5,218 gzip → 400.

## D2 — route taken

**Route 1.** Route 2 is circular and I proved it rather than assumed it: three zlib streams differing only in their last four bytes, handed to `decompress-zlib:git-zlib` in-ship. Correct Adler-32 → `[~ [10.223 5.206]]`. Zeroed Adler-32 → crash. No trailer → crash. The pier log printed zlib's own `-3 / incorrect data check`. The jet validates the checksum over output you do not have yet.

## D3 — input bound

**262,144 bytes** on the member and on the declared ISIZE. Measured cost: ~12 µs/output byte to 250 KB, doubling above. A body at the bound is 4.42 s end to end; one byte over is refused in 32 ms without inflating. Covers ~5,200 pkt-lines; only bites between 256 KiB and git's 1 MiB `postBuffer`.

## D3 — fail closed

**32/32.** 415 for `deflate`/`br`/`zstd`/`GZIP`; 400 for bad magic, CM≠8, reserved FLG, missing NUL, every truncation, ISIZE mismatch, ISIZE over limit; 200 for FNAME/FCOMMENT/FEXTRA/FHCRC singly and together. No `content-encoding` → unchanged path. **No crash** — no `crud`/`bail`/`%hunk` in the pier log across the run.

## D4 — other body paths

- **`v2-command` was the real trap.** A `git fetch` gzips its **`ls-refs`** POST at 1,047 bytes while its `fetch` POST is 288 — the small one compresses first. Decoding only inside `parse-upload-request` would have misrouted it. Decoding happens once at the top and binds `body`; no `u.body.request.req` left in either Git handler.
- **`receive-pack`: git never gzips it.** Six measured pushes — 325 / 479 / 901 / **1,750** / **9,151** / **61,764** bytes — all plain. The 1,750-byte one settles it: past the threshold, same client, same session, uncompressed. Applied the decoder anyway and tested by hand; gzipped and plain pushes give identical object sets.
- **Webhook left alone deliberately**: the HMAC is over the raw body, so decompressing first would break every signature that works today. Both current failure paths are already clear errors.

## D5 — evidence

| repo | refs | proto | request | exit | objects | fsck | hash |
|---|--:|---|--:|--:|--:|---|---|
| gz1 | 201 | v0/v2 | 5,142/5,218 **gzip** | 0 | 600 | clean | identical to source |
| gzreal | 60 | v0/v2 | 1,506/1,579 **gzip** | 0 | 1,204 | clean | identical to source |
| gz2 | 18 | v0/v2 | 936/1,023 plain | 0 | 54 | clean | identical to source |

Shallow + `--unshallow` pass on both protocols over seven gzipped POSTs. All 19 conformance vectors pass; the 18 pre-existing `mug`s match `PUSH-DEFECTS.md` §4c exactly.

## Left undone

- **`handle-upload-pack` answers git's 4-byte flush probe with 400** — same class as push defect 2, needs `http.postBuffer` below the request size to reach, not a gzip defect. Recorded in §6, not fixed.
- CRC32 is not verified (no CRC32 in the desk); three other checks stand in, and the gap is shown by test rather than assumed.
- No repository with >5,200 refs was built to test the bound in anger.

Two commits on `feat/progress-and-joinall`, not pushed. The proxy I started (PID 2562362) is stopped; `~/piers/joinall-bus` is still running as PID 2519792 with the fix installed and my instruments removed.
